children.text: Media Operation Team Suggestion Box: Monthly Analysis Report, Page 10
When are we going to make original content?

This employee appears to have a somewhat puzzling fixation on "original content," seemingly unaware that the "cost-benefit principle" is the gold standard for the team's decision-making. That said, in the interest of maintaining team morale, it is recommended that the team promote the "cost-benefit principle" in a positive light and avoid heavy-handed suppression of such opinions.
I don't like any of the content the team is making right now.

This employee appears to suffer from an excess of creative ambition, failing to recognize that all of our products are made for the audience, and that audience demand is the sole standard for the team's content creation. It is recommended that frontline management strengthen communication to help team members develop a proper understanding of this principle. If necessary, the individual may be guided toward transitioning to an independent content creator, rather than remaining within the team.
Wearing uniforms to work in this blazing heat? That's just torture.

This employee appears to misunderstand the importance of a unified dress code in fostering team identity. It is recommended that frontline management conduct targeted communication on this matter, framed around the "cost-benefit principle," to help team members understand that standardized uniforms enhance the team's efficiency, which in turn increases their individual income.
The packed meals at night are stone cold. Can we get a food warming cabinet?

This employee seems to have mistaken the team's office for their own home, where furniture can be purchased at will. The team is already equipped with a microwave oven, which everyone lines up to use daily with impressive efficiency. In all fairness, it is possible that this employee is unfamiliar with how to use the microwave, or has not noticed that one is available near their work desk. It is recommended to strengthen communication and guidance on the use of the microwave oven.

This round of feedback from the suggestion box reveals that our communication of the "cost-benefit principle" still has considerable gaps that urgently need to be addressed. In addition, the volume of lifestyle-related feedback has exceeded expectations. The root cause likely stems from frontline employees having insufficient work. It is therefore recommended that their workload be increased to prevent them from obsessing over trivial lifestyle concerns.
